keyDates.text: OBBBA student loan changes take effect: GradPLUS eliminated for new borrowers; Parent PLUS capped at $20K/year; new Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) becomes only IDR option for new borrowers
OBBBA tiered endowment tax kicks in for institutions on a July fiscal year: rates rise to 4% or 8% depending on endowment per student; Brown, Cornell, Dartmouth, Penn watch threshold closely
Workforce Pell Grant program takes effect, expanding federal Pell eligibility to approved short-term training programs of 150-599 clock hours in high-demand fields
DHS Duration of Status (D/S) elimination rule expected to take effect for new F-1 and J-1 visa holders; new students must complete programs within four years or apply for USCIS extension
ED accreditation overhaul (AIM framework) final regulations anticipated; could reshape federal oversight of academic institutions and compel adherence to administration policy priorities
Financial aid antitrust trial begins for remaining defendants Cornell, Penn, MIT, Georgetown, and Notre Dame; 74,000+ students already submitted claims in $320M settlement fund
Federal FAFSA deadline for 2025-2026 academic year; students should file before this date to maximize aid eligibility ahead of July 1 loan program changes
Trial date in State of New York v. Department of Education: 19 states challenging Title VI certification requirements as violations of separation of powers and the Spending Clause

charts.title: Estimated Annual Endowment Tax Burden Under OBBBA (AEI Estimates, FY2026)
charts.footnote: Estimates based on five-year IRS Form 990 data and projected endowment growth. Actual liability depends on investment performance and institutional behavior. Cornell, Dartmouth, and Brown fall below the top-tier threshold under current enrollment and endowment levels.

charts.title: University Federal Settlements With Trump Administration (2025)
charts.sourceText: Daily Northwestern / Inside Higher Ed, November 2025
charts.footnote: Columbia figure is $221M total ($200M to U.S. Treasury + $21M EEOC fund). Brown's $50M is a 10-year workforce development commitment, not a direct payment to Treasury. Cornell's $60M is split evenly between Treasury payment and agricultural research investment. Penn and UVA paid $0 but made policy concessions.
